title: Second-Order Thinking
coreMove: Trace what the first result will cause next before choosing the attractive move.
sourcePressure: The official framing centers on consequence chains and the question And then what. The plan must stay practical and avoid unsupported systems-theory sprawl.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says think long term or make a bigger pros-and-cons list.

sourceAnchors.name: And then what
sourceAnchors.detail: the official article frames second-order thinking around consequence chains and the question And then what
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The first answer is only the door; And then what is how you find the room behind it.

tryThisNow: make a pros and cons list

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a town manager considering higher beach parking fees
exampleSpecs.stakes: a revenue win may push cars into residential streets and anger year-round residents
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Amelia traces the first-order revenue gain into the second-order spillover of cars filling side streets before the council vote
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sand stuck to a parking meter coin slot

exampleSpecs.audience: a restaurant owner switching to cheaper delivery containers
exampleSpecs.stakes: unit savings may create soggy food, refunds, and worse reviews
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aidan follows the cheap container from packing line to twenty-minute delivery and writes the refund chain before approving the order
exampleSpecs.firstImage: steam beading under a clear plastic lid

exampleSpecs.audience: a lab manager tempted to waive a glove-change step to save time
exampleSpecs.stakes: one faster protocol may normalize contamination risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Astrid asks the team to name what the shortcut teaches next week's interns before signing off
exampleSpecs.firstImage: purple nitrile gloves piled beside a sample rack

exampleSpecs.audience: a blood bank coordinator adding gift cards to increase donations
exampleSpecs.stakes: today's signups may crowd out repeat donors or attract poorly screened donors
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida asks what happens after the first surge and checks repeat-donor retention before scaling the incentive
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of gift cards beside a mobile-clinic cooler

exampleSpecs.audience: a newsroom growth lead planning a ninety-nine-cent trial
exampleSpecs.stakes: trial growth may train readers to churn before full-price renewal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Chidi draw the second-order renewal behavior behind the first-order signup spike and change the cancellation timing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a renewal curve printed beside a half-finished headline budget

exampleSpecs.audience: a recreation supervisor buying a cheaper chlorine supply
exampleSpecs.stakes: short-term savings could cause cloudy water, closures, and lost swim lessons
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Javier traces the cheaper order through storage, dosing, water clarity, and parent refunds before changing suppliers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: test strips drying on the pool office counter

skillTargets: trace first-order benefits into second-order costs
ask And then what on a concrete choice
evaluate when later effects reverse an attractive move

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one attractive action. Ask And then what three times, writing only visible consequences a real person would have to handle.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
